To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) soil properties (clays, organic matter and soil water content at different dates) can be used to delineate a field into management zones; 2) a multivariate geostastical approach (Factor Kriging Analysis) allows the identification of one factor at longer scale, and the delineation of the field into management zones based on the temporal stability of the soil water content spatial pattern.
the multivariate geostatistic approach, applied to soil properties and temporal stability of soil moisture, allowed us to delineate management units in a durum wheat field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the delineation of MZ using soil properties and multivariate geostatistics and with the identification of MZ based on temporal stability of soil properties.
a new approach for delineating MZ, which is based on a multivariate geostastical method, Factor Kriging, and on soil water content temporal stability.
the delineation of MZ using multivariate geostatistics.

the multivariate geostatistics is a useful tool to delineate management zone and to identify the temporal stability of soil properties.
the FKA approach is an efficient and powerful tool for delineating management zones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multivariate approach is a powerful tool to combine data from various sources in delineation of MZ.
soil properties and a multivariate approach can be used to delineate MZs, which are stable in time and can be used in precision agriculture to optimize fertilizer and water management.
the delineation of the management zones using soil properties, and a multivariate approach may be a useful tool for precision agriculture, especially when soil water content data are available.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil properties and soil moisture can be used to delineate zones for site-specific management.
the delineation of MZs is a complex process that requires a careful selection of the most appropriate soil properties, the best spatial sampling scheme and the most suitable statistical methods.
